claim: Workflow output is not durable merely because a job produced it; GitHub directs operators to upload output as an artifact, and upload/download exposes SHA-256 digest validation.
direct_evidence: “Use artifacts to share data between jobs in a workflow and store data once that workflow has completed.” The validation section says upload-artifact returns a SHA256 digest and download-artifact recalculates and validates it.

incentives.conflicts: GitHub sells hosted automation but the guidance describes an auditable platform contract.

reproducibility.method: Create a workflow-local file, omit upload, then compare a later-job/fresh-run read with an upload/download control.

rights.use: Short quotation with attribution; no source snapshot redistributed.

source.title: Store and share data with workflow artifacts

validity_horizon.trigger: Review earlier if GitHub changes artifact major versions, digest behavior, or runner persistence semantics.

claim: An agent checkpointer backed only by process memory loses every checkpoint when that process restarts; production recovery requires a persistent checkpointer.
direct_evidence: The troubleshooting section states: “MemorySaver and InMemorySaver store checkpoints in RAM. When the process restarts, all checkpoints are lost.” It directs production users to a persistent checkpointer.

incentives.conflicts: LangChain publishes the framework and associated hosted services, so architecture guidance may favor its persistence products.

reproducibility.method: Emit the same completion receipt from two subprocesses; keep one payload only in memory and atomically persist the control payload, then read after exit.

rights.use: Short quotation with attribution; no source snapshot redistributed.

validity_horizon.trigger: Review earlier on LangGraph persistence API or MemorySaver behavior changes.

claim: A production multi-agent research system treats checkpointing and resumability as necessary because minor system failures can otherwise be catastrophic and restarting loses costly progress.
direct_evidence: Anthropic writes: “Without effective mitigations, minor system failures can be catastrophic for agents,” then says it built resume-from-error behavior with “retry logic and regular checkpoints.” The same article says the lead agent saves its plan to Memory because long context can be truncated.

incentives.conflicts: The vendor is presenting lessons from its own commercial system and has incentives to emphasize both capability and engineering maturity; raw incident data is not supplied.

reproducibility.method: The architectural mechanism can be tested by process interruption with memory-only versus durable result state; the vendor's production incidence rates cannot be reproduced from the article.

rights.license: Copyright Anthropic; no open-content license identified
rights.use: Short quotation and link for research only; no article snapshot redistributed.

claim: Across 1,642 annotated traces from seven multi-agent frameworks, researchers identified recurrent failure classes that include loss of conversation history, unexpected conversation resets, information withholding or ignored input, incomplete verification, and premature termination.
direct_evidence: The v3 paper reports “1642 annotated execution traces collected from 7 popular MAS frameworks” and a 14-mode taxonomy. Its taxonomy names FM-1.4 “Loss of conversation history” and FM-3.1 “Premature termination”; FC2 reports unexpected resets and breakdowns in critical information flow.

incentives.conflicts: Academic authors benefit from novelty and adoption of MAST; the paper reports κ=0.88 but this unit did not audit labels or rerun annotation.

reproducibility.method: Obtain MAST-Data and rerun taxonomy annotation and framework-level frequencies against the published protocol.

claim: A public LangGraph bug report alleges that parallel checkpoint writers can silently lose writes because put_writes performs a non-atomic read-filter-rebind-extend operation; the report supplies a small concurrent reproduction.
direct_evidence: Issue #8115 states that PregelLoop.put_writes “has a race condition that causes silent data loss in checkpoints during parallel execution” and shows the shared-list filter, assignment, and extend sequence. It remains open with bug/external labels and no maintainer confirmation.

incentives.conflicts: The reporter authored a proposed fix and therefore has contribution incentives; commenters include unverified reproductions and one service solicitation. None is treated as maintainer validation.

reproducibility.method: Force all writers to take the same pending-write snapshot before publishing, then compare an unprotected rebind with a lock spanning the full critical section.

rights.license: Issue prose is a GitHub-hosted user contribution; repository code is MIT
rights.use: Minimal quotation and linked analysis; fixture is independently written.

source.title: Race condition in PregelLoop.put_writes() causes silent checkpoint data loss

validity_horizon.trigger: Review on maintainer triage, closure, linked fix, or a new LangGraph release.

claim: At the pinned current LangGraph source commit, one put_writes path still rebinds checkpoint_pending_writes from a filtered list and later extends the shared list without an evident lock in that method.
direct_evidence: Pinned _loop.py lines 434-457 contain `self.checkpoint_pending_writes = [w for w in self.checkpoint_pending_writes if w[0] != task_id]` followed later by `.extend((task_id, c, v) for c, v in writes)`; no pending-write lock appears in the file search.

incentives.conflicts: Repository maintainers have incentives to ship a reliable framework, but current source is stronger evidence of implementation shape than issue prose. Actual call concurrency was not established by static inspection.

reproducibility.method: Inspect blob 3710377685c15edb5d27de6f41f182cebafec5b4 at commit f09cfe8ffc1eeffd68f4b628ed69c30f7cad229f; separately establish actual concurrent call paths before applying the causal conclusion to LangGraph.

rights.use: Short code excerpt for analysis; local fixture is independently implemented.

validity_horizon.trigger: Review on any modification to _loop.py or issue #8115.

claim: An external proposed fix wraps the checkpoint pending-write critical section in threading.Lock, but its pull request was closed unmerged and its included negative test cannot prove loss because it asserts only that loss is non-negative.
direct_evidence: Commit 4d7a78c adds `_pending_writes_lock` and wraps put_writes. PR #8114 says an eight-thread stress test had zero loss, but the added test for the buggy path ends with `assert total_lost >= 0`, which passes even when no loss occurs; the PR is CLOSED with no merge commit.

incentives.conflicts: The author is the issue reporter and proposed-fix contributor. The unmerged state and vacuous negative assertion materially lower confidence in claimed framework-level verification.

reproducibility.method: Apply the lock to the exact pinned framework version and replace the vacuous assertion with deterministic schedule and end-to-end graph checkpoint completeness tests.

rights.use: Patch inspected and linked; no patch content redistributed.

source.title: fix: add threading.Lock to PregelLoop.put_writes() to prevent TOCTOU race condition

validity_horizon.trigger: Review if the PR reopens, a successor patch merges, or maintainers reject the concurrency premise.
